text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of symmetrical upper and lower limb weakness, double vision (diplopia), and difficulty climbing stairs, in the absence of sensory changes or fever, strongly points to a neuromuscular junction disorder. The requested MRI scans ruled out compressive spinal cord or nerve root pathology, and your lack of recent infection makes autoimmune causes like Myasthenia Gravis the leading diagnosis.
